title: Energetics in daemonic work extraction protocols via non-ideal QND-energy measurement
authors: Daniele Morrone, Francesco Albarelli, Vittorio Giovannetti, Mauro Paternostro, Marco G. Genoni
abstract: We address the problem of extracting work from a quantum system assisted by a quantum non-demolition (QND) energy measurement. When a perfect QND measurement can be performed and an auxiliary zero-temperature bath is available, the full energy of the quantum state can in principle be extracted even without any prior information on the input state. Owing to the presence of a zero-temperature bath, this is achieved at no energetic cost for the measurement process itself. On the contrary, here we consider what happens when the same protocol is implemented in non-ideal scenarios, specifically when the auxiliary bath has a finite temperature. In this case, not only is it impossible to extract the entire energy from the system, but the measurement strategy also acquires a non-zero energetic cost, accounting for both the interaction between system and measurement apparatus, and the corresponding Landauer erasure cost. We quantitatively assess the performance of these work-extraction protocols, both in absolute terms and through the so-called daemonic net gain, which explicitly includes the energetic cost of the measurement. We rigorously prove that, when access to a thermal bath is allowed in the extraction protocol, the daemonic net gain is always non-positive for any temperature of the auxiliary bath. Conversely, when only unitary operations are considered, the daemonic net gain can attain positive values. We further discuss these different figures of merit by analyzing a paradigmatic example for a single qubit system.
summary: This paper analyzes the thermodynamics of work extraction assisted by quantum non-demolition measurements in the presence of thermal noise. It establishes that while perfect measurement allows full energy extraction, finite temperature introduces an energetic cost, leading to a non-positive net gain when thermal baths are utilized. The key finding is that a positive work advantage can only be achieved if the process is restricted to unitary evolution, highlighting the thermodynamic cost of measurement itself.
main_problem: The paper investigates the energetic cost and feasibility of extracting work from a quantum system using a Quantum Non-Demolition (QND) energy measurement, especially when the measurement process is non-ideal due to a finite-temperature auxiliary bath.
main_result: When a thermal bath is accessible during extraction, the daemonic net gain is proven to be non-positive, indicating no thermodynamic advantage. Conversely, restricting the process to unitary operations can yield a positive net gain.
method: The analysis uses theoretical tools like ergotropy, non-equilibrium free energy ($F_ eta$), and the concept of 'daemonic net gain' to quantify work extraction under different thermodynamic constraints.
model_or_system: The model involves a quantum system ($S$) coupled to an auxiliary system ($A$) for QND measurement, operating within the context of a thermal bath ($B$) at temperature $T=1/ eta$. The analysis compares ideal (zero-temperature) versus non-ideal (finite-temperature) measurement protocols.
key_observables: Daemonic net gain ($\Delta E_{	ext{net}}$), Ergotropy, Non-equilibrium Free Energy ($F_ eta$), and the energetic cost associated with measurement and resetting.
important_parameters: Bath temperature ($ eta$), initial state coherence, and the comparison between unitary vs. bath-assisted operations.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the applicability of the free-energy bound for isothermal work and compares protocols under the assumption of a single bath temperature controlling noise and cost.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the QND measurement protocol and show the temperature dependence of the net-daemonic-ergotropy gain ($\Delta E_{	ext{net}}$) relative to the bath temperature $ eta$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the ideal case (zero-T bath), then analyzes the non-ideal case with finite temperature, deriving the net-daemonic-ergotropy gain. It rigorously proves the non-positivity of this gain when the bath is accessible, contrasting this with positive gains achievable under purely unitary constraints.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous thermodynamic resource theory framework for quantum measurement, quantifying the fundamental energy costs associated with extracting work from quantum correlations, which is highly relevant to quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
